title: PowerToys bug report, as per software's prompt "PowerToys Run ran into an issue. Something went wrong. Please file a bug in the PowerToys GitHub reposi..."

design_decision.reason: The stack trace is useful, but the version mismatch means the safest next step is one fresh current-state diagnostic.

confidence.rationale: The stack trace gives a real lead, but the report still needs live install-state confirmation.

judgment.rationale: The issue provides a useful FileNotFoundException for Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent inside PowerToys Run ETWTrace.Dispose, but the issue form and pasted exception text disagree on the installed PowerToys version.
evidence: The exception text shows TraceEvent missing during ETWTrace.Stop/Dispose.
Local PowerLauncher code instantiates ETWTrace and references the ManagedTelemetry project that carries the TraceEvent package reference.
The issue form says 0.101.2362.0 while the pasted exception text says 0.100.2.0.
judgment.recommended_action: Request one fresh bug report plus exact current version confirmation before choosing between packaging, deployment, or defensive telemetry fallback work.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys fix may be needed, but the current report still needs one live-state confirmation to choose safely between missing-package and mixed-update causes.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys Run reported a missing TraceEvent assembly after update, but the issue currently mixes two different PowerToys versions and does not yet prove whether the install is partially updated or missing a packaged dependency.
known_information: The attached exception originates in ETWTrace.Stop/Dispose inside PowerToys Run.
Local source shows TraceEvent is brought in through the PowerLauncher.Telemetry -> ManagedTelemetry project chain.
The issue form says 0.101.2362.0 while the pasted exception text says 0.100.2.0.
inferences: The failure may be a mixed-version or incomplete-update state rather than a pure code-path bug in ETWTrace itself.
A defensive code change is plausible, but it would be premature to pick it without confirming the live installation state.
issue_context.analysis: The issue already contains a useful stack trace. The specific missing pieces are the exact current version/build and a fresh diagnostic captured from the current installation immediately after reproduction.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the issue body and pasted exception text.
Reviewed local PowerToys Run startup/disposal code and the project-reference chain into ManagedTelemetry.
Confirmed TraceEvent is still referenced from ManagedTelemetry.csproj.

information_gaps.information: The exact PowerToys version shown in About or the installed package immediately after the failure.
information_gaps.why_needed: The report currently shows both 0.101.2362.0 and 0.100.2.0, which changes whether the likely cause is packaging or partial update state.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with the exact version text shown in PowerToys About or the installed package metadata after reproducing the error.

information_gaps.information: A fresh PowerToys diagnostic ZIP captured immediately after reproducing the Run error on the current install.
information_gaps.why_needed: The current-state logs should show which PowerToys Run binaries and telemetry assemblies were present after the update.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce once, then add a comment containing /bugreport immediately afterward. If the normal UI cannot open, run BugReportTool.exe from the PowerToys installation directory and attach the generated ZIP.

comment.body:
Thanks for attaching the exception text — the missing "Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent" assembly is a useful clue. Please provide:

1. The exact PowerToys version currently shown in About or in the installed package after the failure, because the issue form says "0.101.2362.0" while the exception text shows "0.100.2.0".
2. A fresh PowerToys diagnostic ZIP captured immediately after reproducing the Run error on the current install: reproduce the issue once more and add a comment containing "/bugreport" immediately afterward. If the normal UI cannot open, run "BugReportTool.exe" from the PowerToys installation directory and attach the generated ZIP.
